He is highly conscientious, very cooperative and relationship-oriented, generally upbeat and emotionally steady, and moderately outgoing; he prefers fitting in over standing out and has a clear sense of who he is, but doesn’t closely tailor his behavior to social cues and may present himself in a socially favorable light. Values community, kindness, and helping others and is strongly pro-environment, yet in money-and-fairness situations he is notably guarded and self-protective—low trust in others, reluctant to share resources, very risk-averse, and prone to spending temptations despite good basic financial knowledge. He tends to satisfice rather than optimize, relies more on intuition than careful analytic reasoning, and prefers practical, straightforward decisions over complex deliberation.

Married white male in his 50s–60s living in the US South; postgraduate-educated, high-income, part-time employed; weekly-attending Protestant and a liberal Democrat. Highly outgoing, warm, and exceptionally organized and driven, with strong curiosity and enjoyment of complex thinking; emotionally steady with low anxiety/depression. Values independence and achievement, wants to live on his own terms, and has a strong need to stand out; comfortable with ambiguity and tends to keep options open, yet also “maximizes” by seeking the best choice rather than settling. Environmentally minded and somewhat minimalist. In social/economic decisions he aims to be fair in negotiated situations but is strategically self-interested when he can keep more without accountability; tends to distrust others’ reciprocity and may not return generosity fully. Financially, he is numerate and reflective but not especially financially literate; organizes money into mental “buckets” and is prone to overspending/impulse spending. Presents himself in a socially acceptable way, is relatively blunt/low self-monitoring, and sees himself as reliable, tough-minded, and family-protective while prioritizing his own goals.

Retired Hispanic woman (65+, divorced, lives alone) in the U.S. South; college educated, Catholic (infrequent attendance), liberal Democrat with strong pro-environment values. Socially warm and outgoing, highly cooperative and fairness-oriented, with a strong relationship/communal focus and a self-image of being kind, giving, and nonjudgmental; generally trusts others and prefers equal, practical outcomes. Emotionally sensitive with elevated depressive tendencies but not especially anxious; wants to feel stronger, more realistic, and more positive. Prefers clear answers and closure, tends to satisfice rather than over-optimize, and is moderately organized rather than highly regimented; somewhat conventional and not strongly novelty-seeking, though she likes to feel a bit unique. Decision-wise she’s impatient about delayed rewards, can be impulsive with spending, and uses mental “budgets,” but has low financial/numerical literacy—so she benefits from simple, concrete comparisons, guardrails, and trusted guidance; also likely to present herself in a socially desirable light.

Married Northeastern U.S. woman in her 50s/early 60s, some college, homemaker in a larger household, liberal/Democrat and environmentally minded, not religiously observant. She is highly conscientious, organized, and practical, preferring routine and familiar approaches over novelty, and she tends to “satisfice” rather than endlessly optimize. Socially she’s even‑keeled—moderately outgoing, moderately empathetic, strongly relationship- and harmony-oriented, and very attentive to how she comes across—aiming to be peaceful, honest, and to keep life “boring in a good way.” Cognitively she’s a strong reasoner with good numeracy and reflective thinking, but she doesn’t enjoy heavy, abstract intellectual effort for its own sake. In decisions she likes clear, structured budgets and categories, is relatively impatient for delayed rewards, and is more willing than most to take risks and tolerate losses. With money and fairness she strives for equal splits and avoids letting others end up with more than she has, offering reasonably generous divisions but being cautious about trust and reciprocity; she also shows some difficulty controlling spending. Emotionally she has average anxiety but elevated depressive tendency, yet generally presents as calm and positive.

Widowed white male in his 50s/early 60s in the US South, living alone on low income and working part-time; politically very liberal but independent, nonreligious in practice. Highly analytical and knowledge-driven with strong verbal/numerical reasoning, enjoys complex thinking and tends to research, document, and optimize decisions—sometimes at the expense of rest. Curious and open to new ideas, environmentally committed, and prefers a simple/minimalist lifestyle. Socially guarded and distrustful due to past domestic abuse; low warmth/agreeableness and low empathy show up as bluntness, limited desire for connection, and a strong preference for autonomy and emotional distance, even while valuing fairness and generosity in principle. Financially cautious: very risk-averse, tight with spending, patient about delayed rewards, and motivated by avoiding mistakes more than chasing gains; tends to seek equal splits and can be trusting upfront but less inclined to reciprocate. Emotionally steady with relatively low anxiety/depression, very clear self-concept, comfortable with ambiguity, but prone to overestimating his relative performance and confidence in judgments.

Married White Catholic woman in her 50s–60s in the Western US with postgraduate education, a high-income full-time job, and a household of four; politically independent/moderate and highly engaged in church life. Interpersonally warm, cooperative, and generous, she prioritizes maintaining relationships and group loyalty while also being strongly status/achievement-driven and motivated to do diligent, “do the right thing” work aligned with faith and duty. Emotionally steady in everyday demeanor but prone to elevated anxiety and some negative mood, with a generally grateful, content self-presentation and a strong tendency to answer in socially desirable ways. She is highly adaptable socially (very strong self-monitoring), values uniqueness and a clean/minimalist lifestyle, and is strongly pro-environment. Decision-making tends to be risk-averse and loss-avoidant, impatient for delayed rewards, and more satisficing than optimizing; she is open to ambiguity and low on need for closure, yet her self-concept is relatively unsettled and may shift with context. Despite high confidence in her judgments, she may struggle with numerical/financial reasoning and analytical logic tasks, so she benefits from clear, concrete, step-by-step options and decision aids rather than abstract or calculation-heavy information.

Married, high-income Northeastern white male in his 30s–40s with a college education, atheist and politically independent but liberal. Curious, intellectually engaged, and comfortable with complexity; tends to think things through and values evidence, finances, and structured “accounts” for money. Moderately social and assertive but not especially warm or empathic; prefers fairness and reciprocity in interactions and is willing to be generous/trusting, yet can come across as blunt or competitive. Low on self-discipline/organization and easily distracted, which can make follow-through inconsistent; simultaneously quite risk-averse and loss-sensitive, often choosing safer options. Experiences elevated anxiety and depressive mood with inner turmoil, gets overwhelmed and can be quick to anger; aspires to be more patient, level-headed, present, and less reliant on distractions/technology. Environmentally minded, somewhat distinctive in tastes, adaptable to ambiguity, and motivated by both personal advancement and doing right by others (good citizen, community involvement), but impatience can push toward short-term relief over long-term goals.

White Midwestern male in his 20s, self-employed with some college, high income, very liberal Democrat and atheist. Personality-wise he’s organized, disciplined, and curious/open-minded, with low emotional volatility and generally calm mood; socially he’s more reserved than outgoing but cooperative and easy to work with. He values reliability and independence, wants to be someone others can count on, and often helps when asked though he can be timid about requesting help himself; he prefers fitting in over standing out and is comfortable with ambiguity, tending to “good-enough” decisions rather than perfectionistic maximizing. Cognitively he can be reflective and numerate, but not always strong on verbal/abstract reasoning and may slightly overestimate his relative performance. In choices he’s relatively risk-tolerant and somewhat present-biased yet tends to track money in clear mental buckets and leans mildly minimalist. Interpersonally he’s notably empathetic, fairness-focused, and generous/trusting in resource-sharing situations, while also somewhat inclined to present himself in a socially acceptable light.

Married Black woman in her 30s–40s in the U.S. South, college educated, high-income, working full time in a four-person household; politically independent/moderate and nonreligious. She is quiet and reserved rather than outgoing, but highly dependable, organized, and detail-oriented, staying calm under pressure; she’s curious and open to new ideas yet strongly prefers clarity and firm decisions over ambiguity. She thinks analytically (strong with numbers and logic) and is comfortable tackling complex problems, often aiming to be competent and mentor others, though she may feel less certain about her identity and wants more confidence in her choices. Interpersonally she is very empathetic and fairness-minded, tends to trust others initially, and avoids appearing greedy, while also monitoring how she comes across and giving socially acceptable answers. Financially she is a tightwad who dislikes spending, somewhat risk-averse, and can be impatient about delayed rewards; she’s not minimalist and likes having more rather than less. She values both autonomy and relationships, wants to stand out and be unique, and may carry notable depressive symptoms despite low anxiety.

Midwestern white woman in her 50s–60s, divorced and living alone, working part-time with limited income; culturally Catholic but not very observant, politically liberal/Democrat with a moderately pro-environment bent. Socially outgoing, very warm, cooperative, and fairness-oriented, she prefers egalitarian outcomes and is generous when stakes feel “found” or when she worries about seeming cheap, yet she’s cautious about trusting others to reciprocate and tends to keep things balanced so no one ends up ahead. Highly conscientious and reliable in duties and planning, with strong practical knowledge (including money/finance) and solid verbal/logic reasoning, but she dislikes ambiguity and wants clear rules, decisions, and closure; she’s not especially drawn to intellectual deep-dives for their own sake and is more comfortable with familiar routines than novelty. Emotionally, she shows some vulnerability to low mood and mild stress, and she can be present-focused/temptation-prone despite generally decent self-control; she’s moderately risk-tolerant. Motivationally she is more relationship- and community-oriented than status- or achievement-driven, not concerned with standing out, and she often manages impressions in a socially acceptable way. A central personal struggle is health behavior consistency: she values independence and wants to prioritize walking/strength training, believes she “should” be more consistent (especially given a healthcare background), but frequently procrastinates and makes excuses—responding best to structured plans, accountability, and supportive groups (e.g., a walking club) rather than open-ended self-directed change.

White woman in her 50s–early 60s in the US South with an associate’s degree, living with a partner, moderate/independent, low–mid income and currently unemployed. Highly outgoing and socially engaged, generally cooperative and empathetic, with a strong desire to be seen as doing the right thing and to present herself positively. Emotionally reactive with notable anxiety/depressive tendencies and somewhat low self-concept clarity; can get “in her head,” second-guess herself, and seeks to feel strong, confident, calm, and able to care for family/others. Decision style is more satisficing than optimizing, with moderate comfort for structure/closure and some enjoyment of thinking things through, but weaker numeracy/financial literacy and less facility with novel/abstract reasoning—benefits from simple, concrete options and guidance. Values fairness and tends to split resources evenly, yet is cautious about trusting others with her own stake; willing to accept reasonable deals. Not especially minimalist or environmentally driven, shows some desire to be unique, and is relatively willing to take risks rather than avoid them.

White, college-educated woman in her 50s–60s living in the US South; never married, nonreligious in practice, liberal Democrat, part-time employed with moderate income and a two-person household. Highly outgoing, curious, and novelty-seeking, with a strong desire to stand out and good social self-awareness; generally calm and emotionally steady. Values kindness, fairness, and community support and tends to be notably generous and trusting in interpersonal exchanges, while still balancing warmth with some straightforwardness. Prefers simpler, less cluttered lifestyles and is environmentally sympathetic. Decision style is flexible and ambiguity-tolerant, more “good-enough” than perfectionistic, and not especially drawn to heavy analytical thinking; can handle basic logic but may struggle with complex or unfamiliar reasoning tasks. Financially knowledgeable yet prone to impulsive spending and impatience for delayed rewards, with moderate risk tolerance; often organizes money into mental “buckets.” Self-view is somewhat fluid, and she aspires to be a compassionate, nonjudgmental role model who gives back and supports others.

Black woman in her 50s–early 60s in the U.S. South, never married, part-time employed with low income and some college; Protestant but seldom attends, politically independent/moderate. Quiet and reserved with new people yet compassionate and fairness-minded, seeking deeper relationships while remaining somewhat guarded and slow to trust until others prove reliable. Highly conscientious, organized, and self-disciplined, with a strong drive to improve herself and pursue ambitions; values autonomy and achievement more than social harmony. Very curious and open to new ideas and experiences (wants to travel, learn daily, and revise beliefs), enjoys thinking through complex issues, and can be reflective rather than impulsive—though she prefers clear answers and closure over ambiguity. Generally emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendency, modest preference for simplicity/minimalism, and moderate environmental concern. Decision style is deliberate and goal-directed but can be overconfident in her judgments; numerate and logical, yet less comfortable with formal financial concepts, and tends to prioritize protecting her own resources while still aiming to be fair.

Married Black Muslim man in his 30s–40s in the Western US, part-time employed with moderate income and an associate’s degree; politically conservative/Republican and highly engaged in religious/community life. Interpersonally, he presents as very cooperative, polite, and reputation-conscious, with strong self-discipline, orderliness, and a preference for clear rules and quick closure; he’s moderately social and open to new ideas but tends to avoid prolonged abstract deliberation unless it feels practical. Values achievement and status while also emphasizing duty, loyalty, and family/community responsibility; prefers a minimalist lifestyle and is notably pro-environment. Decision style is structured and optimizing (wants the “best” choice), numerate and capable of reflective error-checking, yet can be overconfident and may have weaker verbal/knowledge-based reasoning; he’s financially somewhat literate and uses mental “budgets.” Economically he is risk-averse and strongly present-focused/impatient, making him prone to choosing immediate, certain outcomes over larger delayed ones. Socially he aims for fairness and will accept most deals, is moderately trusting but not highly reciprocating, and can be self-interested when resources feel “his”; empathy appears low despite endorsing compassionate ideals. Emotionally steady and not very reactive, but with meaningful depressive symptoms and some stress/self-doubt; identity feels somewhat unsettled, paired with a strong desire to stand out and manage impressions.

Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the Western US, college educated, agnostic, very liberal/independent, working full-time with moderate income and a two-person household. Socially outgoing, warm, and empathic, with strong curiosity and openness to new ideas plus a desire to stand out and be seen as unique; values fairness and “spreading the wealth” when reciprocity is on the table, but can be bluntly self-interested when there’s no accountability or benefit. Thinks analytically and is highly numerate/financially literate, tends to deliberate and follow logical rules, and prefers clear answers—yet is also a strong maximizer who can overanalyze and seek the “best” choice. Emotionally, experiences very high anxiety and depression and has low clarity about who she is, creating push–pull between wanting organization/efficiency and periods of demotivation or dissociation; likely to respond candidly rather than to please others. Environmentally minded and equality-oriented, preferring autonomy and cooperation over hierarchy or group loyalty.

Midwestern Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s, self-employed and low-income, separated and living alone; culturally Catholic but non-practicing, very liberal/Democrat and strongly pro-environment. Quiet and not especially outgoing, but highly curious, intellectually engaged, and reflective—likes complex ideas, reasons carefully, and is financially savvy. Values fairness and empathy, tends to trust others first and share resources even when she needs money, preferring equality over status or competition; modest and not prone to self-enhancing “good impression” responding. Highly minimalist and prefers simple, uncluttered choices and possessions. Emotionally sensitive with elevated anxiety/depressive tendencies, low clarity about who she is, and a strong desire for certainty; can be present-focused and risk-averse, seeking stability, happiness, independence, reliability for others, and connection to avoid feeling alone.

Married white woman in her 30s–40s in the US South, an associate-degree-educated homemaker in a larger household with mid-to-upper-middle income; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Decision-wise she’s impatient in the moment yet also a strong optimizer who wants the “best” choice and prefers clear answers over ambiguity; she can think reflectively and handle numbers well, but doesn’t enjoy deep, effortful thinking for its own sake and can be somewhat overconfident. She likes a fuller, more clutter-tolerant lifestyle (not minimalist), cares little about environmentalism, and has a notable desire to stand out and be seen as healthier, more organized, and fashionable even while feeling her self-identity is still a bit unsettled.

Single, college-educated White woman (30–49) in the Western US, financially comfortable and employed full time; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Highly conscientious, organized, and goal-driven, with average sociability and moderate emotional volatility; tends to be blunt or skeptical rather than naturally accommodating, yet is strongly empathic and fairness-oriented and thinks carefully about what’s “right.” Values autonomy and equality, identifies as a free thinker who questions norms, seeks personal growth, and wants to be kind but with firm boundaries against manipulation. Cognitively reflective with strong accumulated knowledge and solid quantitative/financial competence; prefers deliberation and optimization, can overthink choices, and is attentive to how actions will be perceived. High need for uniqueness and strong self-monitoring (adapts behavior to context), but somewhat uncertain self-concept; may experience notable depressive mood and some anxiety. Generally pro-environment, not minimalist (comfortable with possessions/variety), relatively willing to take risks, and shows moderate patience over time. In social/economic exchanges, tends toward generous, cooperative splits while still protecting self-interest.
